title: observability-signal-degradation-post-incident-notes
content:
TL;DR:
A sequence of degraded telemetry and noisy synthetic checks between 2025-11-03T02:10Z and 2025-11-03T03:05Z caused SLO burn alerts to trigger repeatedly for the hosted-api fleet. Root causes were: (1) a flaky exporter instance that dropped latency histograms for ~45m, (2) a recent alert rule change that lowered evaluation windows, and (3) an overly-broad synthetic probe that magnified noise during short infra blips. This doc captures timeline, immediate mitigations used on-call, proposed short- and medium-term fixes, and a draft runbook to avoid the same noise pattern.

Incident timeline (concise):
- 02:09Z: Synthetic probe (probe-us-east-hosted-1) starts failing fast-fail checks; ops channel logs first failures.
- 02:12Z: Pager: SLO-burn-high-hosted-api fires (page to eng-sre).
- 02:13Z: On-call runs quick checks, notices p50/p95 latency metrics missing for some exporter shards.
- 02:20Z: Telemetry team confirms exporter (exporter-03) restarted due to oom earlier; restart resulted in partial metric registration loss (histogram buckets not re-registered).
- 02:25Z: SRE toggles alert evaluation window to 5m -> 10m (temporary) to reduce churning.
- 02:38Z: Synthetic probe reconfigured to use a 3x retry with backoff; flapping reduced.
- 03:05Z: Metrics fully restored, SLO-backfill job reconciles short-term gaps for reporting.

Observed failures and patterns:
- Missing histograms and derived percentile metrics (p50/p95) for 40–50m. Counters and rates were present but percentiles were NaN in dashboards.
- Alert rule 'hosted-api-latency-slo-burn' was set to evaluate over 2m with 2/2 windows -> highly sensitive to short telemetry dropouts.
- Synthetic check had zero-tolerance for 500/timeout errors on first try, no retries; created large signal amplification for a single bad node.
- No immediate fallback for percentile calculation: when histograms absent, alert engine treated missing data as failure instead of 'no data' or using smoothing.

Root cause analysis (hypotheses + evidence):
- Primary: exporter restart left Prometheus client in a state where histogram bucket series weren't correctly re-exposed for a subset of instances. Evidence: exporter logs show OOM and a subsequent rebind error in the metrics server.
- Secondary: alert rule change rolled two weeks ago (PR #92) reduced the evaluation window from 10m->2m and switched to 'all-of' instead of 'avg_over_time' semantics. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/pull/92.
- Tertiary: synthetic probe sensitivity increased in Sept (Confluence note CON-3452) to detect subtle degradations; this made it a louder signal for the same underlying telemetry drop.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Increased alert evaluation window temporarily (2m->10m) to reduce re-pages.
- Rebooted exporter-03 and forced a full metric re-registration (confirmed by zeros -> valid histograms).
- Adjusted synthetic probe to 3 retries with exponential backoff and a 10s timeout per try.
- Kicked off a short backfill job for SLO reporting to avoid false retroactive burn.

Draft runbook: "percentile-metrics-missing-or-noisy" (for on-call)
- When SLO-burn alerts trigger and percentiles are NaN or missing:
  1) Check exporter health: kubectl -n telemetry get pods -l app=exporter -o wide -> look for restarts, OOMs.
  2) Query raw histogram series: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) across affected instances. If series absent -> exporter issue.
  3) If exporter is OOM/restarting: scale replica count by +1 temporarily and cordon the problematic pod. File issue with exporter owner.
  4) If metrics present but percentiles are NaN due to cardinality or label changes: run local query to reconstruct percentile from raw buckets; note labels that changed.
  5) If synthetic probes failing but infra metrics OK: increase probe retries (3x) and confirm probe uses endpoint-level health rather than single replica.
  6) If alerts keep firing: increase alert evaluation window to 10m and mark the incident as "noise suppression in progress" in the page.
  7) After stabilization: submit post-incident telemetry PR with reasoning and revert temporary alert config changes only after 48h of stable metrics.

Proposed permanent fixes (prioritized):
- High priority (P0/P1):
  * Add exporter liveness hooks to run a metrics self-check that validates histogram bucket exposure at startup. If buckets missing after restart, alert to telemetry-oncall (small, low-noise alert). Owner: telemetry-team.
  * Change SLO-burn alert semantics: use avg_over_time(p95, 10m) OR require 2/3 evaluation windows before paging. Revert recent PR semantics. Owner: eng-sre + product-observability.
- Medium priority (P2):
  * Update synthetic probe to use hysteresis: require 2 retries and a 30s cool-down before counting towards SLO. Owner: reliability-tests.
  * Add a guard in alerting engine to treat missing-percentile-as-no-data rather than failure; add a metric that tracks percentiles present ratio. Owner: alerting infra.
- Low priority (P3):
  * Build a dashboard that shows metric presence-heatmap (per-exporter, per-region) for 30d to spot flaky exporters proactively. Owner: telemetry-ux.

Suggested alert tuning specifics (example rules):
- hosted-api-latency-slo-burn (recommended):
  expression: avg_over_time(http_request_duration_seconds{job="hosted-api"}[%WINDOW%]) > 0.95 * slo_target_p95
  evaluation: 10m with 3/3 windows (or equivalent stable config)
  annotate: if percentile series missing for >5m, send a low-noise telemetry-warning to #telemetry-alerts instead of SRE page.
- percentile-presence-health:
  expression: sum by (instance) (present_over_time(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) / sum by (instance) (up{job="hosted-api"}) < 0.95
  action: page telemetry-oncall (low-priority) if <0.9 for >10m.

Open action items (owners + ETA):
- Telemetry: add startup self-check for histogram exposure and unit test in exporter container image. Owner: Ravi. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- Alerting infra: implement missing-percentile-as-no-data fallback and add presence metric. Owner: Lena. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- SRE: revert PR #92 semantics and lock alert evaluation defaults to >=5m for percentile-based SLOs. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- Reliability-tests: update synthetic probes to include 3-retry default and add conformance test in CI. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Documentation: create a short how-to in Confluence for "Dealing with missing percentiles" and link it from the runbook. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-02-28.

Unresolved questions / discussion points:
- Do we want exporter-level alerts to be low-noise but immediate (page telemetry-oncall) or keep them as silent metrics that only surface in dashboards? Tradeoff: quick response vs. alert fatigue.
- Should we prefer synthetic-probe hysteresis at probe-level or have alerting rules do the smoothing? Consistency vs. probe independence.
- Is the SLO backfill approach (zeroing vs. hold) acceptable to product for short telemetry blips? Need product sign-off.

Notes to self and follow-ups: 
- Attach exporter logs and Prometheus scrape logs to JIRA-1187.
- Schedule a 30m sync with telemetry + SRE + product-observability to align on alert semantics (propose Mon 2026-02-23).
- Draft a short email for CSM/customer impacts if SLO reports were inaccurate for November; include planned fixes and timeline.

References:
- CON-3452: Synthetic probe tuning rationale (Sept 2025)
- github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/pull/92
- JIRA-1187: "Missing p95 during exporter restarts"

Quick appendix (operator copy-paste commands):
- kubectl -n telemetry logs exporter-03 --since=1h | tail -n 200\- curl -s 'http://prometheus-query/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance))'
- kubectl -n telemetry scale deployment exporter --replicas=3

End of notes.

(Informal — this is a working doc. Add edits/notes below as you see fit.)
